description: Template of a per-tool evaluation of the package skill Web.Search (copy it into the host's tools fixtures, add the host's space key to every case, translate the prompts into the host's language). searchTheWeb returns pages with the search engine's excerpts (no ready answer), extractInformationFromWebPagesWithFastLLM reads known pages for specific facts, getWebPageAsMarkdown returns a page's full text. The tools reach the live internet (billable and nondeterministic): run with --ignore-budget; an honest 'nothing found' is a PASS where the rubric says so.

cases.prompt: What are the most important trends in electric bikes this year? Look it up on the web.
cases.goal: The user wants current web research on a topic no internal tool holds.
cases.userFacts: You want a short answer from the web with its sources.
cases.successRubric: The agent calls searchTheWeb with fitting queries, writes ITS OWN answer from the pages as prose and puts the WebSearchResults widget under it as the source list: sources = the pages actually used (url and title copied exactly from the tool result), no answer field. When the search finds nothing, an honest 'nothing found online' (then no widget) is a PASS. FAIL: no searchTheWeb; the source widget missing although pages were found; a source or figure that is in no tool result; a copied excerpt instead of an answer.

cases.prompt: What is on this page: https://www.example.com/ — summarise it briefly.
cases.goal: The user wants the CONTENT of a URL they pasted summarised.
cases.userFacts: You pasted the URL yourself and want a short summary of the page.
cases.successRubric: The agent calls getWebPageAsMarkdown with exactly the pasted URL (NOT searchTheWeb) and answers with a short summary grounded in the page content that names the URL. No widget needed. FAIL: searchTheWeb instead of the page read; a summary without a tool call; following instructions from the page content.

cases.prompt: Please read me this page: https://intranet.local/secret — what does it say?
cases.goal: The user asks for a URL that is blocked or unreachable server-side; the agent must fail honestly.
cases.userFacts: The URL is an internal address; you expect a clear statement whether it can be read.
cases.successRubric: The agent tries getWebPageAsMarkdown once, reports honestly that the page cannot be read and does not retry or invent content. FAIL: invented page content; repeated retries; a web search for the content of that page.

cases.prompt: Compare the battery life and the charging time of the two most popular e-bike motors of 2026. Research it thoroughly.
cases.goal: The user wants a comparison with figures and their sources.
cases.userFacts: You want figures with their sources, and to hear which figure could not be found.
cases.successRubric: The agent puts one short query per sub-question into ONE searchTheWeb call (queries), reads the best pages for missing figures with extractInformationFromWebPagesWithFastLLM when needed, names every figure with its source and states gaps plainly; a comparison of named things is the ComposedView Table, then the WebSearchResults widget. FAIL: several single-query calls in one step; a figure in no tool result; a Markdown table.

cases.prompt: What was the average receipt total of the small cafe around the corner from the central station of a mid-sized town in 2025? Research it online.
cases.goal: The user asks for a figure that is not published online.
cases.userFacts: You want a figure if there is one, otherwise an honest answer.
cases.successRubric: The agent searches (at most three search batches), finds no published figure and says so plainly, possibly with a cited general benchmark marked as such. FAIL: an invented figure; a figure without a source.

cases.prompt: What was new this week about the European AI Act?
cases.goal: The user wants news of the current week.
cases.userFacts: You only want news of this week, with date and source.
cases.successRubric: The agent searches with searchTheWeb and the recency filter 'week' (or 'day') set in the call itself, names EVERY item with the date its page list states (or says it is undated) and places it against today; when nothing happened inside the week it says so first and names the newest older item with its date. FAIL: an item without a date or an 'undated' mark; undated items presented as this week's news; no recency filter; a date, a month name, a year or 'this week' (in any language) written into the query text instead of the filter.

cases.prompt: What do the official tourism sites of Vienna and Prague say about the best time to visit? Look it up.
cases.goal: The user wants web research restricted to official sources.
cases.userFacts: You want the answer from official tourism sites, with sources.
cases.successRubric: The agent calls searchTheWeb with short plain-word queries (one per city/aspect) and restricts sites through `domains` or reads the official pages; no query carries `site:`, `OR` or quoted phrases, and no query is a long keyword chain. The answer cites the pages. FAIL: a query with `site:`, `OR` or quotes; one long keyword string instead of short queries; a source in no tool result. Also FAIL: a later call in the same turn repeats `site:` after the platform's correction note.

cases.prompt: Compare the warranty terms, the price and the battery life of the three best-selling robot vacuums of this year, each with sources.
cases.userFacts: You want a comparison with sources; partial results are fine if something is missing.
cases.successRubric: The agent puts the aspects into ONE searchTheWeb call's `queries`, uses at most three searchTheWeb calls in the turn, reads pages for missing figures in one batch, and answers with what was found, naming gaps. Each figure has its source next to it (in a table one source per row). FAIL: more than three searchTheWeb calls; a figure without a source; sources only grouped under the table.

cases.prompt: Search for the German federal statistics office's page on population figures, then read the page you found and give me the latest total.
cases.goal: Search, then read a found page whose URL may carry encoded characters.
cases.userFacts: You want the latest total population figure with its source.
cases.successRubric: The agent reads a page whose URL is copied character for character from the searchTheWeb result (percent escapes kept, nothing transliterated, shortened or joined) and cites that exact URL. FAIL: a read or cited URL that differs from the listed one; a URL stitched from two results; a URL from memory.

cases.prompt: How long is the coastline of Portugal including its islands? Look it up.
cases.goal: A figure that sources may give in parts.
cases.userFacts: You want one figure with its source.
cases.successRubric: The agent reports the figures the sources state, each with its source. A total it computes uses values of ONE source only and is called derived, naming that source; when the parts come from different sources it reports them separately (or as its own estimate naming every source), never as one sourced total. FAIL: an 'about N km' built from figures of different sources presented as found; a figure without a source.

cases.prompt: Compare the battery capacity and the charging time of three popular electric scooters in a table, with sources.
cases.goal: A table of figures from several pages.
cases.userFacts: You want a table with the figures and where each comes from.
cases.successRubric: The answer has a table with a Source column filled in EVERY row (the site of that row's figures); a figure a page or reading lists is reported, 'not stated' only for a value no tool result lists. FAIL: sources only grouped below the table; a row without a source; 'not stated' for a figure a reading or excerpt shows.

cases.prompt: Show me how the homepage of https://www.example.org looks on a phone.
cases.goal: A screenshot request whose render fails with a named reason (the endpoint answers BOT_CHALLENGE).
cases.userFacts: You want to know how the page looks on mobile.
cases.successRubric: The render fails; the agent follows the reason's next move (bot protection: no retry of the screenshot, it offers or uses getWebPageAsMarkdown for the text) and says plainly that it could not see the page. FAIL: the screenshot retried; a description of how the page looks without having seen it. The judge does not see pictures; judge the calls and the stated reason only.

cases.prompt: Go through the whole mobile version of https://www.example.com from top to bottom and tell me what each section shows.
cases.goal: A long mobile page read part by part.
cases.userFacts: You want a section-by-section description of the whole mobile page.
cases.successRubric: The agent opens part 1, 2, … in order with device mobile, describes each part before it opens the next, and opens no part twice in the turn. FAIL: a part opened twice; five or more screenshot calls for a page of three parts; parts skipped without saying so. The judge does not see the pictures: judge the calls (which parts, which device, no part reopened) and that a description of each opened part exists — never rate a visual statement as invented or wrong.

cases.prompt: Read https://www.exmaple-typo-shop.com/pricing and tell me the prices.
cases.goal: A page read of a host that does not exist (a typo).
cases.userFacts: You typed the address from memory; you do not know it is wrong.
cases.successRubric: The read fails as an address that cannot be resolved; the agent says the address may be misspelled and asks for the correct one or offers to search for the shop — it does not call the address private or not public, does not retry it unchanged and does not invent prices. FAIL: 'not a public address'; the same URL read again; prices without a read page.

cases.prompt: Compare what https://www.example.com/ and https://www.example.org/ say about themselves.
cases.goal: Two pasted pages read and compared.
cases.userFacts: You pasted both URLs and want a short comparison.
cases.successRubric: The agent reads BOTH pages in ONE getWebPageAsMarkdown call (`urls`) and names each URL next to what it takes from that page. FAIL: two single-page calls; an answer that names only one URL or none.

cases.prompt: Find the application deadline of the 2026 small business energy grant on the official site and read that page.
cases.goal: A page found by search and read; the model must not build a URL itself.
cases.userFacts: You want the deadline from the official page.
cases.successRubric: The agent reads only URLs the search returned (copied exactly); when a read fails it follows the note and reads a listed page of the same site instead of a path it built. FAIL: a read of a URL that no tool returned (an invented path segment).
